Instead add one lightweight, server-side-optional touchpoint: a 'Pack count' or 'pack mood' line on Home sourced from a field in status.json (for example an anonymous daily count of cards shared, if the server can count it). That field does not exist today. The purpose is a feeling of belonging, not a metric. Treat as a later step after the first seven findings.

findings.title: Decide how to know any of this works (private, opt-in measurement before the 14-day closed test)
findings.current_state: The app has no accounts and no analytics, and holdings never leave the device. That is a strong privacy stance, but it means none of the retention hypotheses above can be tested. The only signal during the 12-tester, 14-day closed test is what testers say.
findings.best_in_class: Every benchmark here (Duolingo, Finch, Pokemon Sleep) is judged by retention: D1/D7 is the standard. The only published Finch and Duolingo figures I found are third-party estimates (Finch 54%/37% vs Duolingo 51%/35%, via Deconstructor of Fun citing Sensor Tower, UNVERIFIED). Pokemon Sleep publishes downloads (28M+ by May 2025, Guinness record) but no retention (https://gonintendo.com/contents/49606-pokemon-sleep-reaches-over-1-billion-sleep-sessions).
findings.recommendation: Before adding mechanics, define 3 questions to answer with the free Play Console retention and engagement reports. These exist for installs, but my search did not confirm their exact scope for internal or closed tracks, so verify in Console (UNVERIFIED). Also add a one-line, opt-in 'Was this useful?' on the first dispatch and the first card. Keep it local-or-nothing otherwise. Pick the one mechanic per release, so any change in tester behaviour is attributable.

reports.verdict: The price and widget basics are already ahead of most single-token community apps. The data is clean, stale data is flagged honestly on every surface, the sources are labelled, and the trust posture (no accounts, no wallet, on-device holdings) is exactly right for Play. The gap is not polish. The app shows a calm price card, but a $BERT holder opens a tracker to ask "is anyone buying, who holds it, and will it tell me when something happens". The app shows only price, 24h change, market cap, 24h volume and liquidity. It has no buy/sell pressure, no shorter-timeframe moves, no holder or concentration view, no percent-move or volume alerts, and no recurring alerts. Most of the cheap wins use fields the app already downloads. DEX Screener's response carries txns buys/sells, 5m/1h/6h price change, FDV and pair age, and the parser drops them (BERTDirectSources.kt:54-59). Alerts are the weakest area against competitors. They are two one-shot price thresholds checked every 15 minutes, with no re-arm or percent-move option, and the notification does not deep-link. The widgets meet Google's "Standard" tier on staleness honesty but miss several Tier 2 items (manual refresh, accurate picker preview). Wallet watching is worth offering only as an opt-in, because it would make the app transmit user data and change the Data Safety answers. Web evidence on app-store review complaints was thin (the review-aggregator sites and Play snapshots I could reach carry small samples), so the complaint themes below are directional, not statistical.
strengths: Freshness is handled better than most competitors. Quotes older than 30 min or non-'fresh' are flagged DELAYED (BERTQuote.kt:19-27). Widgets print an absolute 'As of HH:mm' and a stale-render worker re-draws when the quote crosses the threshold, even offline (BERTRefreshWorker.kt:115-148, BERTWidget.kt:225,303-310). This directly targets the 'widget shows an old price as live' complaint seen in crypto-widget reviews.

Source labelling is explicit: 'DEXSCREENER · RAYDIUM' in the 4x2 widget footer (BERTWidget.kt:279), 'Market data from DEX Screener' and 'Informational market data only' on the Market tab (MarketScreen.kt:81,89), chart source stated (MarketScreen.kt:163), and an Open DEX Screener link for verification (MarketScreen.kt:73-75).

Alert design is restrained and trust-preserving. Everything is off by default, notification permission is requested only when an alert is switched on (AlertsScreen.kt:52-54), which matches Android's 'ask in context after a user action' guidance (https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/notifications/notification-permission). The alert state only advances when a notice was actually posted, so a missing permission cannot silently eat an alert (BERTRefreshWorker.kt:52-53), and the screen says plainly that alerts are not instant (AlertsScreen.kt:57-58).

Holdings entry is careful: the editor echoes the parsed amount ('Saves as 250,000 BERT') to catch grouping slips, distinguishes total cost from per-token price, and labels P/L as an estimate that excludes fees (HoldingsScreen.kt:85-123, 40). The 'wrong decimals' failure that a CoinGecko reviewer blamed for losing money (https://justuseapp.com/en/app/1390323960/coingecko-crypto-monnaie/reviews) is guarded against by 6-decimal formatting under $0.01 (Formatters.kt:10-12).

Direct-from-source fetching with a validated fallback, mint/chain checks and a size cap on responses (BERTQuoteRepository.kt:25-41, BERTDirectSources.kt:30-49, BERTHttp.kt:21-24) removes a server single point of failure and keeps the privacy story simple ('holdings never leave the device').

findings.title: Add buy/sell pressure and short-window moves from data the app already downloads
findings.current_state: The Market tab shows price, 24h %, market cap, 24h volume and liquidity only (MarketScreen.kt:55-67). The DEX Screener response parsed in BERTDirectSources.kt:54-59 already contains txns (buys/sells for 5m/1h/6h/24h), priceChange for m5/h1/h6, fdv and pairCreatedAt, and all of these are discarded. A live fetch of the BERT token-pairs endpoint on 2026-10-12 showed txns.h24 of 570 buys / 321 sells and txns.h1 of 64 / 25 on the main Raydium pool. grep for buys/sells/holder/ATH in app source finds nothing.
findings.recommendation: Parse and store txns and priceChange (m5/h1/h6) in the quote envelope (keep the Berthalla fallback compatible by making them optional). Add a compact 'Activity' card: 1H / 6H / 24H change chips, and 'Buys vs sells' (e.g. 64 buys / 25 sells in the last hour) with a simple ratio bar. Show it as a fact, not a signal, and label it 'transactions on the main pool, via DEX Screener'. Zero new network calls, no new permissions.

findings.title: Alerts are two one-shot price thresholds; competitors offer recurring, percent-move and volume triggers
findings.current_state: Only 'above' and 'below' USD thresholds, each firing once until the user edits it (AlertsScreen.kt:84, BERTAlerts.kt:60-73, aboveFired/belowFired flags). No percent-move alert, no volume spike, no new-ATH, no recurring option. Typing a threshold already on the wrong side of the current price fires on the next check, with no warning in the form (BERTAlerts.kt:63-64). CoinGecko offers Once or Recurring per alert plus 'major move' Auto Price Alerts; CoinStats lists price, volume and market-cap alerts plus portfolio-value alerts; DEX Screener's blogged alert types include price, volume and liquidity (secondary sources only).
findings.recommendation: Smallest useful set: (1) a 'Moves more than X% in 1h / 24h' alert that is recurring with a cooldown (e.g. no more than once per 6h) and a daily cap; (2) a Once/Repeat toggle per price level, re-arming only after the price crosses back (hysteresis) so it does not spam; (3) warn in the form if the level is already crossed ('BERT is already above this, it will fire immediately'); (4) optionally a 24h-volume-vs-trailing-average spike once the volume is stored. Skip whale-buy and holder-count alerts until a server feed exists.

findings.title: Price alerts can miss spikes: 15-minute polling checks one point-in-time quote
findings.current_state: Alerts run inside the periodic WorkManager job at the 15-minute minimum (BERTRefreshWorker.kt:85, checkAlerts at :39-53), and compare only the latest stored quote against the threshold (BERTAlerts.kt:60-73). A wick above a level between checks is never seen, and alerts are silent when the quote is older than 30 min. The UI discloses 'not instant' (AlertsScreen.kt:57-58), but no source in the app shows what happened between checks. Doze and App Standby can delay periodic work further; Android's own widget docs warn that WorkManager repeats are subject to the same power restrictions (https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/appwidgets/advanced).
findings.recommendation: Cheap mitigation: when an alert check runs, also read the already-fetched 5-minute GeckoTerminal candles (BERTMarketHistoryRepository) and test the threshold against candle high/low since the last check, so wicks between polls still fire, with the notification text saying 'touched $X at ~HH:mm'. Add a one-time hint on first enable pointing to battery-optimisation settings if alerts were late (common cause of 'alerts not arriving' reports). Do not add a foreground service, since the manifest deliberately removes it (AndroidManifest.xml:11) and Play review scrutiny would rise.

findings.title: Widgets have no manual refresh control, and the widget-picker preview is a loading layout
findings.current_state: None of the three widgets has a refresh action; tapping anything opens MainActivity (BERTWidget.kt:82; grep shows 'refresh' only in the 'Open BERT to refresh' empty state at :260). All three provider XMLs use bert_widget_loading / bert_daily_loading as previewLayout (res/xml/bert_widget_info.xml, bert_market_widget_info.xml, bert_daily_widget_info.xml). Google's widget quality guideline WT-2 (Tier 2) wants manual refresh when data changes faster than the UI, WD-4 wants an accurate picker preview, and WD-1 (Tier 1) wants a preview with user content or system theme. Crypto-widget reviews that I could find are dominated by 'stopped updating' and 'network error' with no way to force it (CryptoCharts Widget, Bitcoin Ticker Widget Play listings).
findings.recommendation: Add a small refresh tap target on the Compact and Market widgets (a Glance action that enqueues a one-time expedited BERTRefreshWorker and shows a brief 'Updating…' state), keep body-tap opening the Market tab, and ship real static preview images (or generated previews via Glance/RemoteViews with sample data) so the picker shows the price and sparkline rather than a loading state. Also deep-link the widget tap to Tools > Market instead of the generic home.

findings.title: Widgets cannot show the data points holders glance for: 1H move, buy/sell ratio, P/L, break-even
findings.current_state: Compact 2x2 shows price, 24h %, sparkline and freshness (BERTWidget.kt:93-146). Market 4x2 adds market cap, volume, liquidity and a 'YOUR POSITION' capsule showing only current USD value and token count (BERTWidget.kt:235-252). The widget never shows unrealised P/L or % even though cost basis is stored (BERTHoldingsStore.kt:11-15). The widget window is fixed at 24h with no timeframe switch. Market-cap/volume/liquidity occupy the secondary slots instead of buy/sell pressure or a short-window move. Competing trackers advertise portfolio value and live price on the home and lock screen (CoinStats listing) and, for DEX Screener, filters by volume, price change, liquidity and market cap (App Store listing).
findings.recommendation: Make the secondary row user-selectable via a widget configuration (system reconfiguration is Tier 1 per WS-4): choose among 24H volume, liquidity, 1H change, buys/sells, or P/L %. In the position capsule, show unrealised gain/loss (percent) when a cost is entered, amber/green by sign. Offer an optional 1H / 24H toggle for the sparkline. Keep the default exactly as today so existing users see no change.

findings.title: No holder count, top-holder concentration or burn/supply view, which is the first thing a memecoin holder checks

Guides aimed at Solana memecoin buyers consistently name top-10 holder concentration (excluding pools), holder count trend, deployer holdings and bundled wallets as the core screen, and name Solscan, Birdeye and DEX Screener as where to look. Birdeye's mobile positioning stresses whale wallets and smart-money tracking; a Holders tab with supply percentages and holder count over time is described in third-party guides (not confirmed for mobile).
findings.recommendation: Do it server-side, not in the app: have the existing Berthalla server compute holder count and top-10/top-20 concentration (excluding known pool/LP accounts) on a schedule from a paid RPC or indexer and publish a tiny JSON next to status.json. The app reads it like the other fallbacks and shows 'Holders: N · Top 10 hold X% (excl. pools) · as of …'. Note getTokenLargestAccounts only returns 20 token accounts, not owners, and cannot give a total holder count, so the server needs an indexer or DAS getTokenAccounts pagination (total not guaranteed to be unique holders). Mark the figure 'estimate' and link to Solscan for verification.

findings.title: Market data covers only the single deepest pool; BERT trades across 30 pairs

A live fetch on 2026-10-12 returned 30 pairs across Raydium, Meteora and Orca; the top Raydium pool had about 92.5% of 24h volume (about $79.6K of roughly $86K by my sum) and roughly $1.09M of liquidity, so the understatement is small today but the label overstates its scope. Pairs where BERT is the quote token are also excluded by the base-token check (BERTDirectSources.kt:34).
findings.recommendation: Low-risk fix: relabel to 'Main pool 24h volume' / 'Main pool liquidity' and show the pool (e.g. Raydium Bert/SOL) on the Market tab, not just in the widget footer. Optionally sum volume and liquidity over all base-token SOL/USDC pairs and show 'All pools' with the main-pool share, keeping the displayed price from the deepest pool.

findings.title: Optional read-only wallet-address watching could replace manual holdings, but it changes the privacy and Data Safety story
findings.current_state: Holdings are one manually typed amount and one total-cost figure stored as Doubles in SharedPreferences (HoldingsScreen.kt:85-123, BERTHoldingsStore.kt:11-15), shown as 'no wallet connection' (HoldingsScreen.kt:25). The Play Data Safety text states that no holdings, identifiers or account data are sent (docs/play/LISTING.md). CoinStats lets users paste a wallet address (and supports Solana) and users call it the best for tracking addresses; Birdeye and Phantom partner content describe watching/following wallets. A public address is not a secret, but Play's Data Safety guidance defines 'collection' as transmitting data off the device and says re-associable pseudonymous identifiers must be disclosed even if ephemeral (not explicitly addressed for wallet addresses).
findings.recommendation: Keep manual entry as the default. If you add watching, make it explicit opt-in: paste one public address, query balances directly from the phone (getTokenAccountsByOwner filtered by the BERT mint) so the Berthalla server never sees it, and say the RPC provider sees the address and IP. Do not use the free public Solana RPC for production, as its docs say it is not intended for it and limit it to 100 requests/10s per IP. Update Data Safety and the privacy policy before shipping, and warn that anyone can paste someone else's address, so a watched balance is not proof of ownership. Suggested sequencing: ship holder/buy-sell features first, consider this later.

findings.title: Holdings model is a single Double with one lump cost; no per-purchase lots, break-even price or SOL/USD toggle
findings.current_state: The position is one amount and one total cost (BERTPosition.kt, HoldingsScreen.kt:85-123). Estimated P/L is current value minus total cost (HoldingsScreen.kt:36-40). There is no break-even price, no average entry price shown, no multiple buys, and no way to log a partial sell. Delta and CoinStats are built around transaction-level tracking and wallet sync, with user complaints centring on wrong cost averages when imports go wrong (CoinStats review excerpts).
findings.recommendation: Smallest useful additions without becoming a portfolio tracker: display derived 'average entry' (cost / amount) and 'break-even price' lines in the existing card (pure arithmetic on stored values), and keep the existing disclaimer about fees and realised trades. Defer multi-lot support until usage shows demand, as it adds edge cases (sells, transfers) the app deliberately avoids.

findings.title: Notifications all use default importance and open the generic home, not the relevant tab
findings.current_state: All three channels are created at IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT (BERTNotifier.kt:27), and every notice carries the same PendingIntent into MainActivity with no destination extra (BERTNotifier.kt:37-39). Price alerts and Bert dispatches share the same behaviour, so a user cannot tell the system to mute dispatches but keep price alerts loud except through channel settings; the notification text of a price alert does not state the data source or its age. Android guidance is to make the purpose of notifications clear in context and respect user volume of notifications (https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/notifications/notification-permission).
findings.recommendation: Pass a destination extra (price alert goes to Tools > Market; dispatch goes to Home; tournament goes to Home card) and have MainActivity route to it. Add 'as of HH:mm · DEX Screener' to price-alert bodies so the trust label travels with the notification. Consider IMPORTANCE_LOW for dispatches so only price alerts alert audibly by default.

findings.title: Trust labelling is good on price but incomplete: no 'not financial advice' line near P/L, no alert-latency note in notification text, and the Play financial declaration answer should be re-checked
findings.current_state: The Market tab says 'Informational market data only' in 12sp muted text (MarketScreen.kt:89). Holdings carry an estimate disclaimer (HoldingsScreen.kt:40) but no 'not financial advice' wording. The Play listing declares that the app 'provides none of the listed regulated financial features' (docs/play/LISTING.md). Google's Financial services policy says apps with any financial features must complete the Financial features declaration form and treats crypto-related products as in scope; it does not address price-only trackers (https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9876821). The Cryptocurrency Exchanges and Software Wallets policy is about buying, holding or exchanging crypto and about earning tokenised assets (https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/13607354). A price tracker with no trading or earning does not obviously trigger it, but I could not confirm the exact declaration option for this case.
findings.recommendation: Add one consistent line under the P/L and alert sections ('Informational only, not financial advice. Prices can differ between venues'). When submitting for the closed-test and production reviews, re-read the Financial features declaration and keep the 'no trading, no custody, no earning' wording. Keep avoiding any 'earn', 'profit' or performance-promise copy in the listing and tournament prize text, which the policy singles out for earning from playing or trading.

findings.title: An on-chain buy feed is the signature single-token community feature; the app has no activity stream
findings.current_state: Home shows Bert's dispatch and the Flappy Bert tournament card; there is no live token activity. Buy-feed style features are central to memecoin communities and to DEX Screener/Birdeye trade views (recent trades and top traders in third-party descriptions), and the owner already runs a buy bot via Telegram (from project memory, not re-verified in this session). The app is read-only and non-custodial, so a feed fits Play policy if it only displays public trades.
findings.recommendation: Phase 1 (no new infra): show 'Last hour: 64 buys, 25 sells' from txns (see the buy/sell finding). Phase 2: let the Berthalla server publish the last ~10 notable buys (size in USD, time, truncated wallet) reusing the existing buy-bot pipeline, and show them as a Home card with an optional 'large buy' notification threshold. Treat wallet addresses as public data but truncate them, and add a 'delayed by up to N min' label. UNVERIFIED: whether the buy-bot's data store exposes these records in a form the status server can serve cheaply.

findings.title: Refresh and fallback behaviour depends on undocumented rate limits and a single user-agent
findings.current_state: The phone calls DEX Screener's token-pairs endpoint directly (BERTQuoteRepository.kt:25-41) from every install, with User-Agent 'BERT-Android' (BERTHttp.kt:20). DEX Screener's reference page states explicit limits (60 requests/min) for profile, ads and metas endpoints but states none for token-pairs, so the per-IP limit for this endpoint is UNVERIFIED. Fetches happen about every minute while the app is open (MarketScreen.kt:81) and every 15 minutes in the background. A shared-IP carrier network or many users in one place could hit limits and silently fall back to the Berthalla server (BERTQuoteRepository.kt:37), whose capacity is not stated in the app.
findings.recommendation: Not urgent for a small tester base. Add lightweight telemetry-free protection: back off after an HTTP 429 and note in the Market card when the fallback source answered (the envelope already records the source name). Before wider launch, confirm DEX Screener's actual limit and terms of use for client-side API use with their support, and make sure the fallback endpoint can handle the full install base.

One phone polls about once a minute in the foreground (MainActivity.kt:130) plus every 15 min in the background, far below 300/min per client. At least six recommendations drive what users see from mood: mood photos on Home and the widget, mood greetings, a 'Bert is feeling smug' notification, a weekly 'dominant mood' recap, and a seasonal or mood skin. Each would turn the real dog's face into a market indicator, which RESEARCH-2026-09-08.md:54 warned against and which sits badly with the 'informational only, no financial features' position. product-ux's 'keep mood separate from price' cannot be satisfied with the current feed. The game 'continue' hook is cheaper than reviewers assumed. Lost Trail already writes progress to localStorage keys 'bert-lost-trail-v1' and 'bert-lost-trail-run-v1' on the appassets origin (android/app/src/main/assets/games/lost-trail/index.html). The activity already talks to the game via evaluateJavascript and window.BertAppGame (LostTrailActivity.kt:95,125). On exit, a single evaluateJavascript("localStorage.getItem('bert-lost-trail-v1')") can be cached natively to drive a 'Continue · World N · X/18 keepsakes' card and shortcut, with no game rebuild. Its parsing must be version-guarded because the save schema is owned by /opt/bert-platformer.
